title: On a new install Library › Memory claims “This changed somewhere else”
criterion: Feature-disabled responses explain the disabled flag; genuine revision conflicts retain conflict recovery.

The UI fix is that describeApiError maps a disabled-feature 409 to category feature_disabled with 'This feature is turned off for this installation.' (describe-api-error.ts:50-52), so stalePage, which needs category conflict, stays false (LibraryMemoryWorkspace.tsx:68) and the false 'changed somewhere else' text is gone. On a default install Library › Memory therefore shows that 'turned off' message in an error callout instead of the memory list, and the callout prints only that summary (LibraryMemoryWorkspace.tsx:200), so it does not say where to turn the setting on. Code read only; the live disabled-flag path was not run (the sandbox has the flag on), and a later task tests it.

note: Chat is retained in React Activity (hidden mode renders at low priority by design). Whether it still re-renders on unrelated navigation needs a React profiler run, which this read-only pass did not do.

title: Chat inspector re-registers on every controller render, doubling renders while open
criterion: Inspector registration is stable across unrelated controller updates.
note: The inspector registration effect depends on `input` and `active`, which the controller recreates on each render, so it re-registers the inspector body on every controller update.

title: Streaming tail re-parses the whole open block each frame; completion remounts it all
criterion: Streaming parsing updates bounded tail content and preserves completed block identity.
note: Streaming now splits the text incrementally and keeps completed blocks memoized with stable keys, but the finished answer is rendered through a different path, so completion may still remount blocks. Not measured.

title: First-run copy speaks release engineering to beginners
criterion: First-run primary copy explains user setup; release proof appears in diagnostics.
note: Live copy on /settings/first-run is plain setup language ('Three steps to connect a model, choose how tools ask for approval, and verify a response'). Release and proof wording is limited to one link at the bottom, 'Open setup and release checks in System diagnostics'.

title: The promised “safe demo” is buried under “Advanced setup and evidence”
criterion: Safe sample exploration is a visible supported first-run action.
note: The demo is a visible peer choice beside 'Use a cloud provider' in step 1 ('Try the demo'), and opens the sample-records panel with plain wording and tour prompts. It no longer sits under an advanced disclosure. Nothing was started in the sandbox.

title: Phone touch targets outside Chat are 28–36 px, and Compact density shrinks everything below 44 px
criterion: Coarse-pointer controls meet 44px product goal; report 24px AA minimum/exceptions separately.
note: Live at 375 px with touch: buttons, selects, tabs and nav links are at least 44 px. Plain text links stay 32 to 36 px (above the 24 px AA minimum, below the 44 px goal) and 'Advanced setup' is 17 px, which is under 24 px. Compact density not tested.

title: Raw IDs, enums, revisions, ISO timestamps and JSON leak into primary UI
criterion: IDs/enums/revisions/JSON are secondary; decision target/scope/uncertainty remain visible.
note: Live, the seven landing pages (desktop and phone) showed no raw ids, ISO times, JSON or enums, and recorded errors go through presentErrorText. Running the raw-values script's own counting (ids inside TechnicalDetails are stripped) on the Cockpit still finds the browser-session actor id printed as visible text in System > Browser sessions (code read, not reproduced live; the sandbox has no browser grant).

title: Tab strips sit above page titles, open on the wrong tab, or hold a single tab
criterion: Area titles precede useful tabs and default/selected tab matches route state.
note: Every area page draws the h1 first, then its tab row, and the default tab (Work Board, Library first tab, System Health) matches the route; screenshots of Work, Library and System show it.

title: Each area uses a different list→detail pattern; most selections aren't in the URL
criterion: Selections use stable deep links and Back restores the selected record with scope guards.
note: Live: selecting a Work task or run, a Library capability or tab, a System tab and a Chat conversation each put the record in the URL and Back returns to the list. In Inbox, 'Review' on an approval leaves the URL at /inbox, so the selection is local state and not a link. The Capabilities row click also left the URL unchanged; that was not investigated (the clicked element may not have been a row).

title: Status encoding is inconsistent and risk badges reuse lifecycle icons
criterion: Lifecycle and risk indicators use distinct consistent icons/text/status tokens.
note: Risk badges use their own Shield and ShieldAlert icons while lifecycle status uses spinner, hand, check, cross and circle, all with text labels; the Work and System screenshots show distinct icons.

title: 'Owner' appears ~45 times, means two things, and never comes with a link
criterion: Owner labels describe the responsible entity and link to a usable record when available.
note: The 45 'Owner' labels are gone from the screens (System now says 'Managed by'). One remains: the memory detail prints 'Owner:' followed by a raw workspace id or 'global', with no link.

title: Results credit 'the Gateway', even for the user's own decisions (48 strings)
criterion: Decision receipts credit the operator action while attributing runtime evidence accurately.
note: git grep finds no result copy crediting 'the Gateway' for an operator decision; settlement text says 'Approved. …'. The two remaining 'The Gateway …' strings (mail-draft-failure.ts:58, :68) describe runtime evidence accurately.

title: Internal consistency-check errors are shown to users verbatim
criterion: Consistency failures explain recovery in readable language with technical details available.
note: Recorded errors pass through presentErrorText: known text is reworded, technical text becomes a neutral line with the raw text kept under technical details.

title: Empty states say what's missing, not what will appear or how to get the first one
criterion: Empty states explain what belongs there and offer an authorized first action.
note: The shared EmptyState takes a title, a description of what will appear and an action, and is used in 60 places (for example 'No Journey events yet' says what will appear). Not every empty screen was checked.

title: Raw provider IDs and an acronym-mangling humanizer ('Mesh mcp server', 'Url')
criterion: Provider/acronym labels preserve established names and do not mangle identifiers.
note: Known cases now have tables (mcp_server reads 'MCP server', mail providers, channels), but humanizeToken itself still lowercases every acronym, so an unlisted token such as 'mesh_mcp_server' or 'url' reads 'Mesh mcp server' or 'Url'.

title: Two-step buttons hide the verb: 'Review apply', 'Review answer', 'Confirm deny'
criterion: Review/confirm buttons state the action and consequences with distinct cancel/commit roles.
note: git grep finds no 'Review apply', 'Confirm deny' or similar; second-step buttons now name the verb and object ('Confirm archive', 'Confirm backup'). 'Review answer' is a composer feature name, not a two-step button.

title: Every border token fails 3:1 and form fields sit on near-identical fills
criterion: Decision-critical control boundaries meet 3:1 in both themes with readable field fill.
note: Buttons, selects, inputs and textareas take --cockpit-border-control (the muted text colour): 5.7 to 6.1:1 in light and 7.8 to 9.2:1 in dark against canvas and raised. The translucent decorative borders (1.3 to 2.8:1) are not used as control boundaries.

title: Most confirm/commit buttons use the secondary variant, identical to Cancel
criterion: Primary commit and Cancel are visually distinct with appropriate destructive treatment.
note: Four confirm buttons now use variant primary (backup, board save, archive in Citadel, local runtime). Three still use the default secondary, identical to their Cancel: project archive, note save/archive, memory promote/reject. Counted over the areas folder; other commit buttons not audited.

title: Reduced-motion reset leaves infinite animations looping at 0.01ms
criterion: Reduced-motion stops infinite decorative animations without hiding activity status.
note: An unlayered reduced-motion rule sets animation: none !important on every cockpit element, beating the older 0.01ms reset in the base layer (cockpit.css:198); the sandbox had no running animation to compare, and status stays as text.

title: Global focus ring is fragile: overridden by unlayered CSS and clipped in scrollers
criterion: Focus rings remain visible through cascade layers and scrolling/clipping containers.
note: The shell-scoped focus ring is unlayered and !important so no other rule strips it, and the tab strip (a scroll container) draws its ring inside with outline-offset -2px. A geometric check of Work flagged only the tab strip and a last link at the scroll edge. The geometric check also flagged 'See History' (clipped by main#main-content); live at maximum scroll its ring (bottom 880) sits inside the scroller (bottom 900), so that flag was not a real clip (b4-GL-33-see-history.png).

title: Surface ladder is nearly flat: light washes out, dark sunken equals canvas (1.06:1)
criterion: Panel hierarchy is readable across both existing themes without replacing fonts/themes.
note: DESIGN-DECISION: The surface values (canvas, raised, sunken, overlay) are exactly the hex pairs in DESIGN.md's colour table (line 30) and line 48 specifies 'Flat surfaces with hairline borders', so the flat ladder (dark canvas to sunken 1.06:1) is the documented design; separation comes from borders.

title: Dark text tiers collapse: secondary is 1.26:1 and muted 1.66:1 from primary
criterion: Ordinary text meets 4.5:1; secondary/muted tiers stay readable and distinguishable.
note: DESIGN-DECISION: The text tiers are exactly the values in DESIGN.md's colour table (line 31). The current values are the documented design and the readability floor is met: every tier is at least 5.2:1 (light) and 7.8:1 (dark) on the surfaces, above the 4.5:1 body-text rule.

title: 92% of sized text is 12-13px; safety copy is 12px muted at ~145-char lines
criterion: Primary and safety copy uses readable size/line length at normal and enlarged text.
note: Measured by characters: 12 px and 13 px text is 86.9% (Inbox), 89.9% (Capabilities), 92.0% (Settings), 94.2% (Library), 95.5% (Chat), 99.2% (System) and 99.7% (Work) of visible text; 14 px is 0% on Work. This is the DESIGN.md-scale body size, so this is a density observation, not a measured safety-copy problem.

title: Heading levels map to random sizes (h1 14-24px, h2 13-20px, h3 13-20px)
criterion: Heading levels use a consistent readable scale and semantic hierarchy.
note: Area pages share one h1 (24 px) and the range narrowed (h2 13 to 16 px, h3 13 to 16 px, h1 14 to 24 px). Chat's h1 is 14 px, and Settings has h2 at 14 px above h3 at 16 px, so a lower level is larger.

title: No Alert/Callout primitive: 220 role=alert lines, mostly bare coloured text
criterion: Shared callouts provide consistent tone/icons/semantics without overannouncing routine states.
note: A Callout primitive now exists (icon, tone, role by tone, quiet option) with 227 uses, but 139 role="alert" lines are still bare coloured text (263 role=alert lines in total, up from about 220).

title: Two dialog systems with different scrims and anatomy; the light scrim brightens
criterion: Shared dialogs provide consistent scrim, focus trap, title and action anatomy in both themes.
note: Both dialog implementations (Radix overlay and native dialog) use one --cockpit-scrim token, defined once for both themes and not lightened in light mode. Anatomy was read, not compared pixel by pixel.

title: No color-scheme: native controls and scrollbars stay light in dark theme
criterion: Native controls/scrollbars follow the effective light/dark color scheme.
note: Live: html and a native select compute color-scheme dark in the dark theme and light in the light theme (also set before paint in index.html).

title: Breakpoints mix rem (CSS) and px (JS) and leave a 639-640px gap
criterion: Shared breakpoint predicates are inverse including fractional widths around 640/1024.
note: CSS and JS both use range media queries on the same px values ((width < 640px), (width < ${RESPONSIVE_BREAKPOINTS.wide}px)). They complement Tailwind's min-width: 40rem exactly at the default 16 px root font size; with a changed root size the rem and px edges would differ by a few pixels. Code read.

title: Six parallel button styles and 10 literal radii bypass Button and radius tokens
criterion: Action controls use legitimate shared button/radius owners without unrelated formatting churn.
note: A shared Button (4 variants, 2 sizes) and IconButton exist and most dialogs use them, but 86 raw <button> elements remain under areas, app and ui, and literal border-radius values (0.4rem, 0.6rem, 0.375rem, 0.75rem, 999px) remain in chat CSS files and gateway-access.css.

title: Cockpit restyles 91 classic/shared class names across three cascade strategies
criterion: Extract actual composition/CSS dependencies while preserving canonical shared runtime owners.
note: Cockpit stylesheets now restyle 67 distinct classic/shared class names (gc-, mc-, mc-next-, mc-gc-) against 91 in the old count, for example .mc-assistant-renderer and .mc-dialog-content. Not operator-visible.

title: Primitives lack disabled styling: disabled menu items and icon buttons look live
criterion: Disabled controls are visibly disabled and cannot invoke unsupported actions.
note: IconButton and Button dim and show not-allowed when disabled, and disabled menu items are marked data-disabled, styled muted and skipped by the click handler.

title: Hints live in native title attributes; Tooltip is used only in the Gallery
criterion: Useful hints are keyboard/touch accessible through shared tooltips rather than title-only.
note: A shared Tooltip is now used in 7 places (including the collapsed rail stream indicator), but IconButton still sets title as its hint and about 345 other title= attributes remain, so touch users see no hint.

title: Disabled-by-default OpenUI renderer (zod/v4 + parser) is loaded and run on every boot
criterion: Disabled OpenUI does not run/load its renderer on ordinary boot.
note: The OpenUI parser and renderer load through React.lazy only when a generated block is shown; live, loading /inbox and /system requested no openui or lang-core modules.

title: @goatcitadel/contracts lacks sideEffects:false; root imports pull zod v3 schemas
criterion: Measured bundle removes unused contract schema graph only after side-effect audit.
note: packages/contracts/package.json now has sideEffects: false, but whether the production bundle drops the unused schema graph needs a build and a bundle analysis; the sandbox is a dev server (it loads zod either way) and builds are out of scope here.

title: Budget script measures the main.tsx stub and index.html CSS, not the cockpit
criterion: Budget measurement counts actual initial Chat chunks/transfer rather than the entry stub.
note: The budget still measures the one entry script named in index.html (450 KB cap). That script is the small main.tsx stub, which loads the Cockpit with import("./cockpit-entry"), so the Cockpit and Chat chunks are only checked by the 900 KB per-lazy-chunk cap.

title: Tailwind scans the whole app dir (classic, tests, mockups) but not the shared pkg
criterion: CSS scan covers actual production/shared consumers and excludes irrelevant sources with visual regression proof.
note: cockpit.css is still a bare @import "tailwindcss" with no source() or @source, so Tailwind scans its default base (the whole app folder, including Classic, tests and mockups). The shared package uses no Tailwind classes, so no styling is missing; the cost is build work and extra CSS.

title: Access gate hides the Gateway's diagnosis and has no retry for 'setup needs attention'
criterion: Access gate shows authoritative diagnosis and a working retry when recovery is possible.
note: The gate's 'Setup needs attention' state now prints the Gateway's own message (access.message) and every non-sign-in state has a 'Try again' button that is disabled only while checking. Code read; the sandbox runs with auth none so the gate cannot be shown live.

title: Returning from classic lands in the wrong area, and Back mixes the two shells
criterion: Classic return preserves intended area/record/history and temporary visit preference.
note: A task detour to Classic opens with shellScope=visit so the saved default stays Cockpit, both shells number history under one key (shell-transition.ts:12) and the shell swap replaces only the current entry, so Back does not mix shells. classicFallbackPath keeps the nearest owner and its query. Code read; the Classic side is out of scope and was not exercised.

title: Unknown and legacy URLs silently render another page under a misleading title
criterion: Known legacy URLs retain IDs/scope/hash; unknown route/record gets explicit not-found.
note: Live: /nonexistent-page shows an h1 'Page not found' and tab title 'GoatCitadel Page not found'; the legacy /ops/approvals?approvalId=abc link lands on /inbox keeping approvalId; /work/runs/does-not-exist shows 'Run details unavailable. That item no longer exists.' Unknown routes no longer render another page.

title: Overlapping homes and vocabulary: 'Board' vs 'boards', Work History vs System Activity
criterion: Work/System retain distinct useful views and describe their purpose without unrequested consolidation.
note: Work keeps 'Board' and 'History'; System keeps 'Activity' and 'Dashboards'. Live headers describe different purposes ('Workspace tasks and recent Chat or supervised plan runs', 'Saved runs, conversations, and recent activity in this workspace', 'Recent signals across this installation'), so the singular/plural clash and the History/Activity overlap are explained rather than merged.

title: Inbox rows can't be triaged without opening each item
criterion: Inbox rows expose risk/expiry/age/target sufficient for triage before opening.
note: Rows now show kind, age, a risk chip, an expiry line and the action name, so risk/expiry/age can be triaged. A shell approval still reads 'Target details are available in the approval record' (commands are deliberately kept out of rows), so the target needs a click.

title: Inbox order and keyboard flow work against fast triage
criterion: Inbox sorts actionable risk/expiry/age and moves focus to a meaningful next item after settlement.
note: Items sort by risk, then expiry, then age (stated on screen: 'Sorted by risk, then expiry, then age'); after a decision focus moves to the next item in the group or the empty state. Code read for the focus part.

title: Single-key Inbox shortcuts are always on and can't be disabled (WCAG 2.1.4)
criterion: Single-character shortcuts can be disabled or are safely focus-scoped without hijacking typing.
note: The keyboard icon in the Inbox header opens a panel with 'Enable Inbox letter shortcuts' (saved per browser); the handler ignores typing in inputs and open dialogs. Shortcuts only move focus.

title: Library lands on a tool catalog titled ‘Library’; governance pages are orphaned
criterion: Library overview explains resources and links governance destinations without disguising tools as the entire Library.
note: /library now opens a page titled 'Candidates and mesh' (no longer a tool catalog titled Library) and the tab row names every Library section. But there is still no Library overview explaining what Library holds, and the only Library page that links to Settings › Citadel is /library/citadel itself (LibraryGovernanceRoute.tsx:33), so the criterion's overview and governance links are not met.

title: Policy inspector needs six technical inputs before it answers anything
criterion: Policy inspector uses available scope/action context and progressively exposes technical inputs.
note: The policy inspector is headed 'Evaluate a selected tool context' and keeps the technical inputs behind an 'Advanced policy context' disclosure, so it answers from the selected capability without six manual inputs.

title: First paint and browser chrome ignore the theme; no 'match system' option
criterion: First frame and browser chrome match the effective persisted/system theme without flash.
note: A pre-paint script sets data-theme from the saved choice, else from prefers-color-scheme, and index.html paints a matching background; the cockpit then rewrites the theme-color meta to the chosen theme. 'Match system' is offered in every theme control. Code read; a visual flash was not captured.

title: Route changes are silent: no focus move, no live announcement, no skip link
criterion: Navigation moves focus/announces meaningful area change and supplies a working skip link.
note: A skip link now exists, is the first tab stop and moves focus to #main-content. But a route change (g then w, or a sidebar click) leaves focus where it was, announces nothing (no live region), and the skip link leaves #main-content in the address bar. Not verified with a screen reader. The nav.afterSkip capture in b5-desktop-m1.json and the skip block in b5-m2.json are superseded by b5-skip-focus.json (the earlier runs tabbed from a stale focus start).

title: Palette shows empty group headings and coverage noise instead of a ‘no results’ state
criterion: Palette hides empty groups and gives a useful no-results state without coverage noise.
note: Groups with no items are filtered out, search coverage sits behind a single 'Search coverage' disclosure, and a query with no hit shows 'No matching commands or returned records' with suggestions. Live: 'zzzqqq' gives no group headings and that line (screenshot).

title: Ctrl/Cmd+1–5 steal browser tab switching, die while typing, and nothing documents them
criterion: Area shortcuts use g then c/i/w/l/s/t outside inputs; ? documents them and palette remains available.
note: Area shortcuts are 'g' then a letter, ignored inside text fields and dialogs, and the '?' dialog documents them; Ctrl/Cmd+K stays the palette. Live: g then w opened Work. Earlier skip-link captures (b5-desktop-m1.json, b5-m2.json) are superseded by b5-skip-focus.json.

title: Toasts sit over header actions, keyboard focus doesn't pause them, errors look like info
criterion: Toast placement avoids actions, keyboard focus pauses expiry, and errors have clear tone.
note: Toasts sit 64 px from the top (below the 48 px header rows) and the realtime attention toast uses toast.error / toast.warning, so failures carry their own tone; the toast library pauses expiry while the stack has keyboard focus. Code read; focus-pause is library behaviour and was not exercised.

title: Navigation context churns each render; 39 consumers and 6+ handoff owners re-render
criterion: Navigation context/handoff ownership stays stable across unrelated renders in profiling.
note: ENGINEERING-NOTE: the navigation provider still builds its context value inline each render (consumers fell from 39 to 11 files); the criterion needs a profile and has no operator-visible symptom, so it is not carried as a finding.

title: Phone and tablet users cannot see which workspace they are acting in
criterion: Phone/tablet shows current Citadel/workspace before scoped actions.
note: Live: at 375 px the Chat page text never names the workspace or Citadel (it appears only inside the More sheet); at 820 px the collapsed rail shows a compass icon with no name (tooltip and accessible name only).

title: Palette can't find common destinations: 'settings', 'approvals', 'health' return nothing
criterion: Palette synonyms find Settings/Approvals/Health and navigate to functional native destinations.
note: Destinations carry search terms: live, 'settings' returns 'Go to Settings', 'approvals' returns 'Go to Inbox', 'health' returns 'Go to System' and 'Go to System > Health'.

title: Inspector doesn't take focus, drops focus on close, and floats unscrimmed on tablets
criterion: Inspector has guarded focus entry/return and correct overlay/scrim on tablets.
note: Below 1024 px the inspector is a modal with a scrim; at 1024-1279 px it floats and takes focus; closing returns focus to the opener. At 1280 px and up the docked panel takes no focus on open (focus is only moved when floating, inspector.tsx:187-189), so a keyboard user must tab through the page to reach it (Ctrl+I only toggles). Code read only.

title: Area nav items are buttons, and several in-area links swallow Ctrl/Cmd-click
criterion: Navigation links preserve Ctrl/Cmd/modified-click browser behavior.
note: Sidebar areas, phone tabs and in-area tabs are real links with an href and let modified clicks through (isModifiedClick, 24 call sites in the cockpit). Code read.

title: Scroll position leaks between areas and sub-pages; Back doesn't restore it
criterion: Area/subpage scroll positions and Back restoration are keyed to route/scope.
note: Scroll position is stored per installation, caller, scope, pathname, search and hash and restored on return, so areas and sub-pages no longer share one offset. Code read.

title: Phone tab bar loses 'you are here' in System/Settings; Back ignores open sheets
criterion: Phone displays current System/Settings and Back closes the top sheet before leaving.
note: Back now closes the open More sheet and stays on the page (live: history.back() with the sheet open left the URL unchanged and the sheet closed). But the More tab only gets aria-current in Capabilities, System and Settings; its colour is identical to an inactive tab (live computed rgb(176,200,213) in Chat, System and Settings), so the visual 'you are here' is still missing.

title: Models › “Get started” tab renders an empty panel
criterion: Models Get started renders existing guided setup content and working next steps.
note: Live: Models › Get started renders the setup summary (three steps, Open setup) instead of an empty panel, and the old /settings/onboarding address lands on the same Models page.

title: Settings search misses everyday words like “dark”, “notification routing”, “ollama”
criterion: Settings search finds common aliases including dark, notifications and Ollama.
note: Live: typing 'dark' or 'notification routing' in Search settings finds General; 'ollama' finds Providers & models. The search terms now include theme, light, dark, notification routing and ollama.

title: Settings is buried in a 24 px gear menu, never shows as current, and 'account' is empty
criterion: Settings is discoverable and current-state is visible; account entry opens real access behavior.
note: Settings shows as current now (aria-current plus a filled gear), and the menu's first item opens Settings. But Settings is still a 24 px icon in the sidebar footer named 'Settings and account', and the menu holds no account entry (Settings, a theme item, Switch to classic).

title: Citadel settings stack 8 undefined fantasy terms plus 'posture' (15+ uses)
criterion: Citadel labels explain branded concepts with plain terms while user/host values remain intact.
note: DESIGN-DECISION: DESIGN.md:69 says 'Plain names first, Citadel names second (Rules · Wards)'. Live: the Citadel tabs read 'Rules · Wards', 'Agents · Council', 'Secrets · Vault', 'Export/import · Blueprint', and the empty state says 'No rules yet'. Enums go through plain-word label tables.

title: Provider change-plan dialog loses primary/destructive styling to unlayered classic CSS
criterion: Provider plan retains primary/destructive styling despite shared/Classic CSS.
note: Measured with the real stylesheets on a dialog-shaped element: with the class chat-change-plan-modal the last (primary) button keeps the neutral grey fill and the destructive one only turns its text red; without the class they are accent and red. The cockpit's rules live in a CSS layer, the classic change-plan CSS is unlayered and wins. The dialog itself was not opened (no pending plan).

title: Card-in-card nesting: three levels of bordered boxes on Settings and System
criterion: Settings/System sections use purposeful consistent hierarchy without nested card noise.
note: DESIGN-DECISION: DESIGN.md:103 forbids a bordered box inside another. Measured live on Models (expanded), General, Safety, Access, Advanced and Citadel: no bordered box sits inside another (deepest nesting 1), sections use hairline separators.

title: Hooks expose raw mutate/intercept modes for every event, unexplained
criterion: Hook modify/intercept controls explain effects and require appropriate risk review.
note: The hook mode select now reads 'Observe only', 'Can change the request', 'Can block the action'; creating or editing a non-observe hook gets a red 'Apply reviewed hook action' review. Code read.

title: Local AI’s main buttons file no-op approvals; real llama.cpp setup is scattered
criterion: One Local AI flow performs real supported setup/serve actions; unsupported actions are explicitly disabled.
note: Live Models › Local AI: the real llama.cpp setup (use a running server or let GoatCitadel start one, Check server, Finish setup) is the first section; the advisory 'Request download/serve approval' buttons are tucked in a closed 'Advisory approval requests (no execution)' disclosure that says they only record intent.

title: Integrations tab hides six unrelated tools behind a toggle and lists records twice
criterion: Integration controls have clear grouping and one record list with useful diagnostics.
note: One 'Saved integrations' list; the management panel says it 'keeps no second list' and opens the chosen connection from that list. The three management views are one labelled segmented control ('Management views'). Code read.

title: The Channels tab cannot disable or remove a channel or delete a draft
criterion: Channels support governed disable/remove/draft deletion with receipts/errors.
note: Channel setup (now Chat › Messaging › Advanced channel setup) has 'Review disable/enable channel', 'Remove channel connection' and 'Delete saved draft', each through a reviewed dialog with a confirmation message. Code read.

title: Danger styling is overused on safe actions and missing on access-widening ones
criterion: Safe actions use normal styling; access-widening actions expose explicit consequence and review.
note: Most red buttons now are delete, revoke, replace or access-widening (TLS skip, hook that changes requests, prompt skipping). One is not: the dialog behind 'Review disable/enable channel' confirms with a red 'Apply reviewed channel change' even when the change is only enabling or disabling.

title: Help text and validation errors are not programmatically tied to their fields
criterion: Help/errors are programmatically tied to fields and announced at the right time.
note: The shared Field wires help and error text to its control with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and Settings uses it in 57 places. The permission profile form still hand-builds some fields: the control has an aria-label and the help line below it is not linked to it.

title: “Budgets” is a cost preference with no runtime effect and no explanation
criterion: Budget UI accurately describes preference behavior without claiming enforced spending limits.
note: Live: the control is titled 'Budget preference' and says 'A saved preference ... This is not a dollar limit' and 'no mode switches models or caps spending today'. The rail description says the same.

title: Revoking a device can disconnect you, but “this device” is never marked
criterion: Current-device revoke is identified and reviewed with disconnect consequence.
note: The device the operator is using is marked ' · This device', and the revoke dialog says 'This can disconnect the current device. A new approval is needed to regain access.' Code read; the sandbox has no device grants.

title: Update channel switches to unsigned preview builds instantly, without confirmation
criterion: Preview update selection requires explicit risk review and never auto-installs/cuts over profiles.
note: Choosing Preview opens 'Use Preview updates?' ('Preview builds from main are unsigned. Checksums do not establish publisher identity. Downloads and installer execution still require your action') with a red confirm and a stale-state guard. Desktop-app only; read from code.

title: Secrets are entered five different ways; webhooks need a keychain ref nothing creates
criterion: All provider/connector secrets use secure inputs and existing custody with real keychain-reference creation where required.
note: Live: New destination › Keychain HTTPS webhook asks for a 'Webhook URL secret reference' typed as free text ('Use existing keychain references'), and nothing on the page creates or lists one. The provider and web-search keys now use secure inputs, so this is the remaining gap.

title: MCP: “Connect” hides in an Inspect sheet; templates sit below manual fields
criterion: MCP templates/guided connect are primary and supported transports/auth/errors are truthful.
note: Register MCP server is a toolbar button now, and the create dialog opens 'Use an advertised template' above the manual fields. Connecting is still inside the per-server inspection sheet, reached through a button labelled 'Connections, tools and transport'.

title: Health cards report counts instead of problems and route every fix to Classic
criterion: Health lists actionable problems/recovery and keeps incomplete evidence visible.
note: Health now sorts checks by severity, words each state and detail (for example 'No managed local runtime is enabled'), keeps unconfirmed checks visible with an 'unverified' count, and links each card to its native owner page rather than Classic.

title: Quality tablist lacks arrow keys and points aria-controls at missing panels
criterion: Quality tabs support arrow keys and reference real accessible panels.
note: Live: on System > Quality, focusing a tab and pressing ArrowRight moves selection and focus to Evaluations, End moves to Design, and every tab's aria-controls id exists in the page. The tabs are Radix Tabs.
